newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ocampo sees Colombia 1997 oil exports at $3.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Ocampo sees Colombia 1997 oil exports at $3.5 bln.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo predicted on Thursday his country would export $3.5 billion in oil this year, assuming a price of $19 a barrel.
"I expect oil exports to total about $3.5 billion at $19 a barrel for the year," Ocampo told Reuters in an interview.

Ocampo, in Paris to court French investment in Colombian infrastructure, said Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol had as yet been unable to resolve how to offer sweeter deals to foreign oil firms unhappy with their current contract terms.
He also acknowledged that guerrilla attacks on pipelines and attacks on foreigners harmed Colombia's potential but said such violence was not as bad a problem today as it had been in the past.
Referring to negotiations with foreign oil firms for sweeter terms, he said, "The issue has not yet been solved. It is under study, but it's difficult to solve for political reasons."
Concerning guerrilla attacks, "This is an old area for them and for us," he said, referring to the foreign oil firms operating in Colombia.

"Unfortunately, there are lots of problems with guerrillas in the oil sector. But violence is not as big a problem now. Ecopetrol has learned very well how to manage the problem, how to respond to attacks," he said.

British Petroleum Co Plc Chief Executive John Browne warned recently that leftist guerrilla activity in Colombia could force it to abandon some of its oil exploration projects in the country, Energy and Mines Minister Rodrigo Villamizar said this week in Bogota.
BP, the single largest foreign investor in Colombia, had conditioned further exploration in the promising Piedemonte block on a beefed up military presence in the area.
